chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Kathir al-Khazzaz, from Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

He said to me: "Do you not enter the market? Do you not see the fruit being sold, and things among what you desire?" So I said, "Yes." He said: "Indeed, for you, for everything that you see and are unable to buy, there is a good deed."

key_terms.السُّوقَ: the marketplace where goods are displayed and sold
key_terms.الْفَاكِهَةَ: fruit, mentioned as an example of desirable goods
key_terms.تَشْتَهِيهِ: that which you desire or long for
key_terms.حَسَنَةً: a good deed recorded as reward

ai.seo_question: What reward does a poor Muslim receive for seeing desired things in the market and being unable to buy them?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that when a poor believer sees desirable goods in the market but cannot afford them, patient restraint is rewarded by Allah with a good deed. It highlights divine mercy toward the poor and affirms spiritual reward in everyday experiences of deprivation.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn Bin Kaseer Al Khazzaz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Would you not like to enter the market and see the fruits and the things from whatever you desire, being sold?’ So I said, ‘Yes’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, for you, with everything what you see and are not able upon buying it, there is a good deed’.
en.sarwar: 17. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Kathir al-Khazzaz who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) asked me, ‘Do you want to go to the market where fruits and things that you desire are sold?’ I said, ‘Yes, 1 like to go.’ The Imam said, ‘However, for everything that you like to buy but cannot buy there is a reward of one good deed for you.’”
